title: Group presentations and word reduction
section: Part B: Abstract Algebra ▷ Generators and Relations
terms: group presentation; generators and relations; defining relation; word in generators.

exposition.text:
A presentation ⟨S | R⟩ describes the group generated by the symbols S, subject exactly to the
relations R and their consequences. Relations permit replacement and simplification of words.
2 2
For example, ⟨a, b | a = b = e, ab = ba⟩ presents the Klein four-group.
n
A relation a = e by itself only implies that the order of a specified element divides n. In the
one-generator presentation with that sole relation, the resulting group has order exactly n. To
prove a presented group has a proposed size, word reduction gives an upper bound; a concrete
group realizing the relations often gives the matching lower bound.

question.text:
4 2 2
What is the order of the group ⟨a, b | a = e, b = e, ab = ba, b = a ⟩?
(A) 1 (B) 2 (C) 4 (D) 8 (E) 16

solution.text:
2 4
Eliminate b using b = a . The remaining relations reduce to a = e, so at most four
elements remain. The cyclic group of order four realizes all relations with a of order four,
proving that the order is exactly four.

question.text:
4 2 −1
What is the order of ⟨a, b | a = e, b = e, bab = a ⟩?
(A) 2 (B) 4 (C) 6 (D) 8 (E) Infinite.

solution.text:
−1 k k
The relation ba = a b moves each b to the right. Every word reduces to a or a b, with
0 ≤ k < 4, so the order is at most eight. A quarter-turn a and a reflection b of a square
satisfy all three relations and generate eight distinct symmetries. This realization gives the
matching lower bound; the relation does not allow replacing b by a power of a.

question.text:
Which group is presented by ⟨a, b | ab = ba⟩, with no other defining relations?
(A) Z × Z (B) Z (C) Z × Z (D) The trivial group (E) S
2 2 3

solution.text:
m n
Commutation reduces every word to a b for integers m, n. Realize a = (1, 0) and
2
b = (0, 1) in the additive group Z ; all such pairs are distinct and satisfy the relation.
Thus no further identifications occur. Commuting generators do not acquire finite orders
without corresponding relations.

(A) 1 (B) 3 (C) 5 (D) 15 (E) Infinite

solution.text:
8 3 7
Conjugating by a three times sends b to b , but a = e makes this equal to b. Hence b = e,

and together with b = e this forces b = e. The presentation reduces to ⟨a | a = e⟩. A
cyclic group of order three realizes the relations, proving the order is exactly three.
